title: Close cleanly, walk away well and track your progress
course_title: Negotiation Skills for Business and Life

say: Close cleanly, walk away well, and track your progress.
This is the video for Module 4 of Negotiation Skills for Business and Life.
Many good negotiations fall apart after the handshake, because each side remembers the deal differently. You said delivery was included. I thought the balance was due next month.
Closing well means making the agreement clear, complete and recorded.

say: You also learn what to do when talks get stuck, and how to prove to yourself that you are improving.

panel.heading: Make the deal hold

Put every key term in writing

say: When gaps get small and the other side asks practical questions, like when can you deliver, move to close. Say, it sounds like we are close. Let me summarise what we have agreed.
Then check every point. Who the parties are, exactly what is supplied, the price, deposit and balance with dates, delivery, and what happens if something is late or faulty. Both sides confirm.
After a phone negotiation, Ronke sends a WhatsApp message the same day. She lists the item: tiers, flavours and design, as in the photo the client sent.

say: 250000 naira in total, including delivery to the hall and setup. She also states when design changes are accepted, and that the deposit is not refundable after materials are bought.
She ends: please reply Confirmed if this is correct. The client confirms and pays, and Ronke checks the credit in her bank app before sending a receipt.

say: A stuck negotiation is not a failure. It is a signal to change approach. First, go back to interests. Ask, what matters most to you here?

say: If you feel angry, frightened or rushed, or the other person becomes aggressive, stop. Leave if you feel unsafe, and return with a trusted person or continue by message.

say: Learn to recognise pressure tactics. A false deadline. My oga must approve, after you have already conceded. Or small extras asked for after you agree.

say: Answer calmly. I understand, I need until tomorrow. Then my offer also depends on final approval. Happy to add that, and it will cost this much more.

say: The landlord wants 1800000 naira for two years upfront.
Another shop two streets away costs 700000 for one year. That is her BATNA. Her walk-away for the first shop is 850000 a year, paid yearly.

card.title: Ebere and the shop lease
rows: Her BATNA: other shop, a year

say: She offers 800000 for one year, then tries paying in two parts. He says two years or nothing. Paying it all at once would empty her savings.
So she closes politely. Thank you, Sir. It does not work for me now, but if anything changes, please call me.
She inspects the other shop, confirms the owner, and keeps 1100000 for equipment and stock. Walking away was a decision based on numbers, not a failure.

say: Keep a log, one line per negotiation. Your score shows how far between your walk-away and your target you landed. 0% is your walk-away. 100% is your target.
Here the walk-away was 27000, the target 33000, and the result 32000. That is 5000 out of 6000, about 83%.
Also rate the relationship from 1 to 5. Over ten negotiations, if your score rises while relationships stay at 4 or 5, you are clearly improving.
To remember. Summarise every term and get it confirmed in writing, with receipts for every payment. Deadlock means change approach, not push harder.
Compare the best offer with your BATNA, and walk away politely when it is worse. And log and score your negotiations.

say: Now your turn. Write a confirmation for a real deal, plan your calm replies to pressure, and start your negotiation log with a 90-day plan for your next important negotiation.
